Card Grading Companies in Canada, Compared

By Nathan Wiebe, CPA — collector, and a buyer and seller of cards. Published July 28, 2026.

There's no single best card grading company for Canadians — the right one depends on the card. PSA carries the strongest resale premium for modern star cards and now has a Mississauga receiving centre that skips some cross-border friction. SGC and CGC are well-regarded alternatives, especially for vintage. Canadian graders like Overtime Grading, TGA, KSA, and HOF Grading avoid the US border trip entirely, which suits lower-value or bulk submissions where cost and turnaround matter more than resale-market recognition.

This guide compares the graders a Canadian collector can realistically use: what actually differs between them, what it costs, how long it takes, and the cross-border friction the US-based graders add that the Canadian ones don't. If you've already decided on PSA specifically, our PSA submission guide covers the three routes Canadians use to submit, and our card grading 101 guide covers whether a specific card is worth grading at all before you pick a grader.

Which Graders Can a Canadian Actually Use?

Four major graders dominate the hobby: PSA (Professional Sports Authenticator), SGC, CGC (Certified Guaranty Company), and Beckett Grading Services, often called BGS. All four are US companies with no Canadian grading facility — PSA is the exception in that it opened a Canadian receiving centre in Mississauga, Ontario, but the actual grading still happens at PSA's US operations. None of SGC, CGC, or Beckett currently publish a Canadian receiving location on their own sites.

Alongside those four, a handful of Canadian-based graders operate entirely inside the country: Overtime Grading (Balzac, Alberta), TGA (True Grade Authentication, Surrey, British Columbia), KSA Certification (Ontario and western Canada offices), and HOF Grading (Hall of Fame Card Grading, Toronto-based, mail-in only). None of them carry PSA's resale-market recognition, but none of them require a cross-border shipment either.

How Much Does Card Grading Cost in Canada?

It depends entirely on the grader and the service tier you pick within that grader — slower tiers cost less, faster tiers cost more, and every grader adjusts pricing over time. We're not going to print a single "card grading costs $X" number here, because it would be wrong for most graders and most cards. Instead, here's what's actually posted on each grader's own site as of this writing, with a link to check the current number yourself before you submit.

Is PSA or SGC Better for Canadian Collectors?

Both are reputable, both are US-based, and both mean a cross-border shipment either way. PSA is the more widely recognized name in the hobby and tends to carry the strongest resale premium on modern star and rookie cards — buyers pay more, on average, for a PSA-graded copy of the same card versus an equivalent grade from another company. SGC has a long history and a loyal following specifically among vintage collectors, where its black-bordered holder is a familiar, trusted sight. Neither is "better" in general; the right pick depends on what buyers of your specific card actually favor.

Do I Pay Customs Shipping Cards to a US Grader?

Potentially, yes — SGC, CGC, and Beckett all grade exclusively at US facilities, so a mailed submission from Canada crosses the border twice, with the customs paperwork, duty exposure, and cross-border shipping cost that implies. PSA is the one exception: its Mississauga, Ontario receiving centre routes Canadian submissions through a bundled customs arrangement instead of taxing each shipment individually, which is a genuinely different experience than mailing cards straight to the US. Our guide to that location covers the address, hours, and how in-person drop-off works. The four Canadian graders below skip this question entirely — nothing leaves the country.

Are Canadian Grading Companies Like TGA, KSA, and Overtime Grading Legit?

Yes, in the sense that they're real, operating businesses with their own certification numbers, tamper-evident holders, and online cert-lookup tools — we've linked each one's actual site and pricing above rather than taking their word for it. What they don't carry is PSA's decades of resale-market recognition, so a Canadian- graded card may sell for less on the open market than an identical card in a PSA holder, purely on brand recognition rather than actual condition. Whether that gap matters to you depends on what you're grading and why:

  • Overtime Grading (Balzac, Alberta) posts CAD pricing directly on its site — $15/$20/$25 CAD per card across three turnaround tiers (30/15/5 business days), with bulk discounts at 100+ cards. It operates out of the same New Horizon Mall location listed in our directory as Overtime Sports Cards & Grading, so Albertans can drop cards off in person.
  • TGA (Surrey, British Columbia) grades sports cards and TCG cards side by side, with tiers from $15/card (15-card minimum) up to $50/card same-day grading by appointment. Its own FAQ notes turnaround can extend beyond its stated target during high-volume stretches — check tgagrading.com for the current estimate before submitting.
  • KSA Certification has operated since 1996 out of an Ontario office and a separate western Canada office, with published tiers running from same-day "Walk Through" service at $150/card down to $15/card for 100+ card bulk submissions.
  • HOF Grading (Toronto) is a mail-in-only Canadian grader with tiers from a 180-day budget option up to a 3-day rush option; current pricing on its site is discounted from posted regular prices, which is worth confirming still applies before you submit.

What About Grading Through a Local Shop?

A number of shops in our directory offer grading services of their own: they take your cards in person and handle the submission — usually to PSA — on your behalf, which takes the cross-border shipping question off your plate entirely. Shops that currently list grading services include 306 Sports Cards in Saskatoon, SK, Cardera Collectibles in Balzac (Rocky View County), AB, and Rival Cards in Ajax, ON. Our PSA submission guide covers that route in full, alongside submitting direct and group submissions.

How Long Does Card Grading Take?

It varies by grader and, within a single grader, by the tier you pick — the same company can run a slow, cheap tier and a fast, expensive one side by side, and posted turnaround times shift with how busy each grader currently is. CGC's own site currently posts anywhere from 2 business days (WalkThrough) to 150 business days (Bulk); Beckett posts 5 to 75+ business days across its four tiers. The Canadian graders above run their own separate timelines, usually faster for a simple reason: cards aren't crossing a border twice. Check the specific grader's current turnaround before you submit — none of these numbers are fixed.

Which Grader Fits Which Situation

If you're grading a modern star or rookie card and resale value depends on maximum brand recognition, PSA is the name buyers pay the most for — worth the border trip, and Mississauga now shortens that trip for Canadians. If vintage is your focus and the card's era matters more than the grading brand, SGC's long vintage-collector following makes it a reasonable alternative worth pricing out alongside PSA. If you're grading a stack of modern bulk or lower-value cards where a resale premium wouldn't cover the extra cost and hassle of a US grader, one of the Canadian options — Overtime Grading, TGA, or KSA's bulk tiers — usually makes more financial sense. And if you'd rather not handle shipping or paperwork at all, a local shop that offers grading services does that work for you.
